question: Can observed Pico historical-loss-affected native taxon richness of five, versus one each at three other islands, be explained solely by Pico having more sampled 10x10m plots (24 versus 10,12,12)?

fixed_design.plot_sampling: uniform sampling without replacement of m already-surveyed independent plot identifiers
fixed_design.original_species_positive_plot_counts_no: Use bound over all possible unknown k_i in [1,N], with exactly T distinct detected native loss-affected species and total positive taxon x plot cells P.
fixed_design.lower_bound: distribute P-T excess into one taxon up to N before moving to next; follows discrete concavity
fixed_design.upper_bound: distribute P as equally as possible across taxa; follows discrete concavity
fixed_design.return: exact Fraction and float lower/upper mean rarefied richness for each island
fixed_design.no_taxonomic_or_site_labels: Only integer plot count N, species count T, total positive plot count P
fixed_design.unit_test: Exhaustively enumerate small occupancy vectors and confirm hypergeometric bound optimizing extrema

primary_interpretation: Bound applies to EXPECTED taxon richness in a random m-plot subset of the already sampled habitat; not every possible subset, no ecological extinction-risk or conservation rescue inference.
incomplete_causal_controls: species historic range size and true extinction dates
